unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes the sentence explaining that a woman's will 'ends by settling the moral'. It also deletes 'she wanted him much to be civilized'. 'Luckily for him' is the answer to the unanswerable question of when robbery and murder become virtue, and without these sentences it reads as a mere transition.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Luckily for him' and the general law survive, so the woman-as-guide theme is still legible.

evidence.quote: Women have, commonly, a very positive moral sense; that which they will, is right; that which they reject, is wrong; and their will, in most cases, ends by settling the moral.
Women have, commonly, a very positive moral sense; that which they will, is right
In July, 1859, she was at Thun in Switzerland, and there Henry Adams joined them. Mrs. Kuhn not only adored Italy, but she cordially disliked Germany in all its varieties.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Women have, commonly…settling the moral' sentence before 'Mrs. Kuhn not only adored Italy'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan says to keep her description and the general law; this sentence is their premise.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The argumentative hinge from the moral dilemma to giving the reins to a woman is lost. The general law then arrives with less earned logic.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Women's moral-sense law cut, so the sister no longer resolves the dilemma

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the sentence on being crushed 'at the points of contact' between worlds and the line 'Of the Germany to come, he knew nothing'. It also cuts 'the moment was decisive for much to come'. The chapter's frame of an eighteenth-century boy meeting modern forces is lost, and 'Suddenly' now opens para 6 with no prior state.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'the eighteenth-century which the Germans were ashamed of' and 'Until coal-power and railways were created' keep some of the contrast.

evidence.quote: He was in a fair way to do himself lasting harm, floundering between worlds passed and worlds coming, which had a habit of crushing men who stayed too long at the points of contact.
He was in a fair way to do himself lasting harm, floundering between worlds passed and worlds coming
Suddenly the Emperor Napoleon declared war on Austria and raised a confused point of morals in the mind of Europe.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'floundering between worlds' sentence at the head of para 6, and optionally 'Of the Germany to come, he knew nothing.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Planning omission: this is a listed recurring mechanism but was not named as protected text.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The young man's ignorance of future Germany is no longer marked as such. The 1859 war loses its framing as a decisive collision of eras.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'Floundering between worlds' and limited-knowledge markers removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept the old man shrinking 'into corners of shame' and the aphorism about the habit of expression. The revision leaves only 'said it not very well', which flattens the double judgment behind 'the nearest approach he had yet made to an intelligent act'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The required closing phrase survives verbatim.

evidence.quote: he shrank into corners of shame at the thought that he should have betrayed his own inferiority as though it were his pride
In after life he shrank into corners of shame at the thought that he should have betrayed his own inferiority as though it were his pride
He had little to say, and said it not very well; but it was still the nearest approach he had yet made to an intelligent act.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the first draft's 'In after life he shrank…as though it were his pride' clause before 'but it was still'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required section; the voice profile asks to keep then-beliefs distinct from later judgment.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The irony of the young man's display of inferiority 'as though it were his pride' disappears. The verdict reads as plain faint praise.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Retrospective shame over the Courier letters cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the clause about 'young men… taking for granted that everything had a cause', for whom Rome was 'the most violent vice in the world'. That clause is the premise later defeated by 'No law of progress applied to it' and by the repeated 'Why!'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'the last place under the sun for educating the young' retains part of the anti-education claim.

evidence.quote: taking for granted that everything had a cause, and that nature tended to an end, Rome was altogether the most violent vice in the world
To young men seeking education in a serious spirit, taking for granted that everything had a cause
For the rest, Italy was mostly an emotion and the emotion naturally centred in Rome. Rome before 1870 was seductive beyond resistance.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence beginning 'To young men seeking education in a serious spirit'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: 'resists any law of progress or sequence'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The paradox of Rome as vice against causal education is lost. The later sequence-denial and questioning lose their set-up.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Rome's premise of cause and end dropped

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops 'The thought of posing for a Gibbon never entered his mind' and 'He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness'. It also drops 'No one ever had answered the question'. The paragraph now opens with 'Even the greatest of men', a clause that in the source justified his being a mere tourist.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'the tourist, who went on repeating' still labels him.

evidence.quote: He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness, and it was well for him that he should be nothing else, for even the greatest of men cannot sit with dignity

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft cut the qualification that Paris 'might serve better purpose than the twenty-one months passed elsewhere'. The revision then also cut 'From the first he had avoided Paris'. That weakens the reversal from disapproval to enjoyment and leaves the accidental-education thread without its last ironic twist.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Disapproval-permitting-enjoyment and the closing phrase survive as planned.

evidence.quote: perhaps, after all, the three months passed there might serve better purpose than the twenty-one months passed elsewhere; but he did not intend it
From the first he had avoided Paris, and had wanted no French influence in his education.
He squandered two or three months on Paris. He disapproved of France in the lump, and shut it figuratively out of his life.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the avoidance sentence and the 'perhaps…but he did not intend it' clause before 'Therewith'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required gist; the restaurant catalogue was optional, but the ledger qualification is a planning omission.
